stories.headline: StrataFlux restores accuracy to 2‑bit LLMs
stories.body: **Precision without the bulk:** StrataFlux streams higher‑precision data from host RAM or SSD to recover accuracy lost to 2‑4‑bit weight and 2‑3‑bit KV‑cache quantization. It keeps the speed and memory wins of low‑bit inference.
stories.why: You can run cheaper LLMs faster without sacrificing results.

stories.headline: NPCBench challenges multimodal cancer reasoning
stories.body: **A new test for AI doctors:** NPCBench bundles 4,777 component items, a 100‑patient cohort, and 417 scored diagnostic and care tasks to evaluate multimodal reasoning on nasopharyngeal carcinoma. The benchmark mimics real clinical pathways.
stories.why: Helps you gauge model performance on real‑world medical data.

stories.headline: Thursday security patches hit five Linux distros
stories.body: **Patch day for the stack:** AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Mageia and Oracle pushed Thursday updates covering dozens of packages. The fixes address a range of vulnerabilities across the stack.
stories.why: Keeps your servers and IoT devices from known exploits.

highlights.title: StrataFlux: Memory-Hierarchy-Native Low-Bit LLM Inference
highlights.summary: StrataFlux is a framework that restores accuracy lost to 2‑4‑bit weight and 2‑3‑bit KV‑cache quantization while keeping the memory and speed benefits of low‑bit LLM inference by streaming higher‑precision data from host RAM or SSD.
highlights.detail: The system co‑designs refinement representation, selection, and delivery so that precision data are fetched only when needed and reused across decoding steps, overlapping transfer with computation. Evaluations were run on dedicated GPUs and unified‑memory platforms, showing that selective precision streaming can avoid generation stalls without large bandwidth overhead.

highlights.title: NPCBench: A Clinical Apprenticeship Benchmark for Multimodal Care-Pathway Reasoning in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma
highlights.summary: NPCBench is a multimodal clinical apprenticeship benchmark for nasopharyngeal carcinoma that includes 4,777 component items and a 100‑patient CarePath cohort with 417 scored diagnostic and care tasks.
highlights.detail: The benchmark moves beyond isolated factual questions by requiring models to integrate guideline knowledge, imaging, and longitudinal patient data across a care pathway. Evaluation measures joint correctness of diagnosis and treatment decisions throughout the episode, aiming to reflect real specialist training.

highlights.title: The Power of Meta Access in the Software of the Future --- Demonstrated on LLM Chat UIs and Chat AI
highlights.summary: The paper proposes meta access, a permissioned, structured view of a chat interface that lets LLM assistants read and modify UI elements, organized into a ladder of capability levels.
highlights.detail: Levels range from feature tutoring to full orchestration, enabling a single chat client to serve as a hub for finding, navigating, and operating the workspace. The authors note new risks such as grounding errors, privacy leaks, prompt injection, and the need for a separate control‑plane to manage reflexive meta access.

items.title: Australian universities are creating AI-native graduates
items.summary: Australian universities are expanding access to ChatGPT and embedding AI tools into teaching to ready students for an AI‑enabled workforce.
items.detail: The initiative includes campus‑wide licensing of ChatGPT and curriculum updates that incorporate generative AI into assignments and labs, aiming to develop graduates who can leverage AI responsibly across disciplines.

items.title: Cult.fit builds operational muscle with Codex
items.summary: Cult.fit is using OpenAI Codex across multiple teams to build internal tools faster and reshape how work is performed.
items.detail: By integrating Codex, developers can generate code snippets, automate repetitive tasks, and prototype applications without extensive manual coding, accelerating product development cycles and improving operational efficiency.

items.title: GPT‑6 Cyber: Advancing the frontier of aligned cybersecurity agents
items.summary: OpenAI announced GPT‑6 Cyber, a cybersecurity‑focused LLM that discovers exploitable vulnerabilities and proposes fixes while remaining within authorized scopes.
items.detail: The model is trained to respect permission boundaries and to generate remediation steps, positioning it as an aligned assistant for security analysts and automated vulnerability management pipelines.

items.title: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash: Fast and cost-effective with longer clips
items.summary: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash is a faster, lower‑cost model that can process longer audio or video clips.
items.detail: The update focuses on reducing inference latency and compute expense while extending the maximum supported sequence length, making it more suitable for real‑time applications. It builds on the previous Omni 1.2 release with optimised kernels.

items.title: New NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Open Models for Interactive World Simulation
items.summary: NVIDIA introduced the Cosmos 3 open models for interactive world simulation.
items.detail: The models are hosted on Hugging Face and target high‑fidelity physics and agent behavior in virtual environments. They are released under an open license to encourage community research and integration into simulation platforms.

items.title: Model: AtomicChat/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-Uncensored-GSQ-RCO-GGUF
items.summary: AtomicChat/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-Uncensored-GSQ-RCO-GGUF has been downloaded 92,333 times and received 330 likes on Hugging Face.
items.detail: The model is listed under the text‑generation category and is part of the trending feed, indicating strong community interest. It is distributed in GGUF format for efficient inference on consumer hardware.

items.title: Model: FusionCow/Sulphur-3
items.summary: FusionCow/Sulphur-3 has 607 downloads and 385 likes on Hugging Face.
items.detail: The model appears in the trending list, suggesting niche popularity. It is provided in a standard repository format suitable for fine‑tuning or direct inference.

items.title: [$] User namespaces + file capabilities = trouble
items.summary: A patch series by Josef Bacik aims to stop privilege escalation from user namespaces to host processes.
items.detail: User namespaces allow containers to appear as root inside the namespace, but the patches tighten checks that previously allowed a process to gain elevated rights outside its namespace. The changes are slated for inclusion in the upcoming kernel release.

items.title: Critical security vulnerability affects OpenSSH on Alpine Linux systems
items.summary: OpenSSH 10.6p2 adds a workaround for a critical vulnerability affecting musl‑libc systems with PAM disabled, such as Alpine Linux, and Alpine will backport the fix to version 3.16 (May 2022).
items.detail: The bug’s root cause lies outside OpenSSH, allowing a rapid mitigation. Developers advise disabling password authentication (PasswordAuthentication=no) or shutting down SSH on affected hosts immediately. The issue does not impact non‑Linux platforms, Linux systems using glibc, or Linux with PAM enabled.

items.title: Memory Fit: Architectural Support for Page Placement by Learning Models of Good Behavior
items.summary: Server main memory is increasingly heterogeneous, incorporating technologies such as zswap, CXL memory expanders, and emerging phase-change memories (PCM). To decide where to place pages, operating systems have to choose…
items.detail: Server main memory is increasingly heterogeneous, incorporating technologies such as zswap, CXL memory expanders, and emerging phase-change memories (PCM). To decide where to place pages, operating systems have to choose between efficient but coarse-grained access bits, out-of-band profiling, or costly runtime instrumentation. This paper proposes memory fit, a hardware abstraction that provides precise and accurate page placement information to an operating system. items.title: xDSL-CCPP: An alternative code generator for atmospheric modelling
items.summary: xDSL-CCPP replaces the original regex‑based Python code generator in the Common Community Physics Package with a DSL‑driven generator to simplify GPU‑focused modernization of atmospheric model physics code.
items.detail: The new generator leverages domain‑specific language techniques to handle the growing complexity of CCPP specifications, enabling more maintainable Fortran output and easier integration of GPU acceleration pathways that the legacy tool could not support.

items.title: SymFC: Configurable Semantics for All Paths Symbolic Execution in Haskell via Embeddings
items.summary: SymFC introduces configurable symbolic semantics for Haskell, allowing all‑path symbolic execution via embeddings to cover IO and larger programs previously unsupported.
items.detail: By decoupling symbolic representations from fixed SMT base types, SymFC can be tuned for specific libraries and constructs, improving scalability and making lightweight verification more practical for real‑world Haskell codebases.

items.title: KOSMOS: Self-scheduling Persistent Kernels for Communication-Compute Overlap
items.summary: KOSMOS provides self‑scheduling persistent kernels that dynamically switch between communication and computation roles, eliminating idle windows in transformer TP+SP and EP workloads.
items.detail: The library queues workgroups by consumer demand, fusing each collective with its GEMM and running an entire expert layer in a single launch per direction, removing the need for pre‑tuned split schedules.

items.title: Per-Query Recall Guarantees for Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search in Dynamic Vector Databases
items.summary: PQR-Search guarantees per‑query recall bounds for ANN search, ensuring the probability of recall falling below a threshold τ does not exceed δ for any query, even after updates.
items.detail: The method stores 1‑bit codes of rotated residuals relative to IVF centroids and relies on a random orthogonal transformation, avoiding distributional assumptions and eliminating the need for retuning after insertions or deletions.

items.title: googleworkspace/cli
items.summary: googleworkspace/cli is a single command‑line tool that accesses Drive, Gmail, Calendar, Sheets, Docs, Chat, Admin and more, built dynamically from Google Discovery Service and includes AI agent skills.
items.detail: The CLI consolidates multiple Google Workspace services into one interface, automatically generating commands from the service definitions, and extends functionality with AI‑driven assistants for common tasks.

items.title: NVIDIA/Model-Optimizer
items.summary: NVIDIA/Model-Optimizer is a Python library that applies state‑of‑the‑art techniques such as quantization, distillation, pruning, NAS and speculative decoding to compress models for deployment frameworks like TensorRT‑LLM.
items.detail: By unifying these optimizations, the library streamlines model preparation for high‑performance inference, supporting multiple backends and enabling faster serving without manual tuning of each technique.

items.title: blacklanternsecurity/bbot
items.summary: bbot is a recursive internet scanner written in Python for security testing.
items.detail: The tool automates crawling and probing of web resources, aiming to help penetration testers map attack surfaces efficiently. It is open source and available on GitHub, with a focus on extensibility for custom modules.

items.title: crmne/zapfast
items.summary: ZapFast is a native WhatsApp client built in Rust using the egui framework.
items.detail: Designed for speed and low resource usage, ZapFast provides a desktop interface without relying on web wrappers. The project showcases Rust's capability for real‑time communication apps and is open source on GitHub.

items.title: dolphin-emu/dolphin
items.summary: Dolphin is a C++ emulator that runs GameCube and Wii games on PC with ongoing improvements.
items.detail: The emulator supports high‑resolution rendering, controller mapping, and networked multiplayer, continuously adding compatibility fixes. It remains a community‑driven project, regularly updated to enhance performance and game compatibility.

items.title: floci-io/floci
items.summary: floci offers a lightweight, free alternative to the AWS Local Emulator.
items.detail: Targeted at developers needing local testing of AWS services, floci mimics core functionalities without the cost or complexity of official emulators. It is open source and aims for simplicity and minimal resource consumption.
